slides.heading: 10 T-codes every ABAP developer *uses daily*
items: SE38 / SE80 - Write and browse programs
SE16N - Look at table data fast
ST05 - SQL trace for slow reports

posts.caption:
Save this list. You will use it every single day.

The 10 T-codes that cover most of an ABAP developer's work:
SE38/SE80 to write code, SE11 for the dictionary, SE16N to check data, ST22 to read dumps and ST05 to catch slow SQL.

Knowing these by heart makes you noticeably faster, and interviewers expect it.

Which T-code do you open first every morning? Tell us in the comments.

slides.heading: Step 1: *Get your data*
slides.code:
SELECT vbeln, erdat, kunnr, netwr
  FROM vbak
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_orders)
  UP TO 100 ROWS.

slides.heading: Step 2: *Create and show* the ALV
slides.code:
cl_salv_table=>factory(
  IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
  CHANGING  t_table      = lt_orders ).

lo_alv->display( ).
slides.note: That's a working ALV. Columns come from the table type automatically.

slides.heading: Step 3: Add the *toolbar*
slides.note: Sort, filter, Excel export and zebra stripes in 3 lines.

slides.heading: Don't forget *TRY...CATCH*
slides.body:
factory( ) raises CX_SALV_MSG, and get_column( ) raises CX_SALV_NOT_FOUND for a wrong column name.

Wrap the ALV code in TRY...CATCH and show the error text.
slides.highlight: Column names must be UPPER CASE

slides.title: Your report is slow because of *THIS*
slides.subtitle: SELECT inside LOOP
slides.voiceover: आपकी रिपोर्ट स्लो है? नब्बे परसेंट केस में वजह एक ही होती है। लूप के अंदर सेलेक्ट।
slides.spoken: Aapki report slow hai? Nabbe percent case mein wajah ek hi hoti hai. Loop ke andar SELECT.

slides.heading: The *slow* way
slides.code:
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order).
  SELECT SINGLE name1
    FROM kna1
    WHERE kunnr = @ls_order-kunnr
    INTO @DATA(lv_name).
ENDLOOP.
slides.voiceover: ये कोड देखो। हर ऑर्डर के लिए, हम डेटाबेस से कस्टमर का नाम पढ़ रहे हैं। दस हज़ार ऑर्डर्स, मतलब दस हज़ार डेटाबेस कॉल्स।
slides.spoken: Ye code dekho. Har order ke liye hum database se customer ka naam padh rahe hain. Das hazaar orders, matlab das hazaar database calls.

slides.heading: Why it *hurts*
slides.body:
Every SELECT is a separate trip to the database.

The loop is fast. The round trips are what kill you.
slides.highlight: Read once, then look up in memory
slides.voiceover: हर सेलेक्ट, डेटाबेस तक एक अलग ट्रिप है। लूप तेज़ है, लेकिन ये ट्रिप्स आपकी रिपोर्ट को मार देती हैं। तो रूल सिंपल है। एक बार पढ़ो, फिर मेमोरी में ढूंढो।
slides.spoken: Har SELECT database tak ek alag trip hai. Loop tez hai, lekin ye trips aapki report ko maar deti hain. To rule simple hai. Ek baar padho, phir memory mein dhoondho.

slides.heading: The *fast* way
slides.code:
SELECT kunnr, name1 FROM kna1
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
  WHERE kunnr = @lt_orders-kunnr
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_kna1).

LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order).
  DATA(lv_name) = VALUE #(
    lt_kna1[ kunnr = ls_order-kunnr ]-name1
    OPTIONAL ).
ENDLOOP.
slides.voiceover: फिक्स ये है। लूप से पहले, एक ही सेलेक्ट में सारे कस्टमर्स पढ़ लो। फिर लूप के अंदर, इंटरनल टेबल से नाम उठा लो। और हाँ, फॉर ऑल एंट्रीज़ से पहले टेबल खाली तो नहीं, ये चेक करना मत भूलना।
slides.spoken: Fix ye hai. Loop se pehle ek hi SELECT mein saare customers padh lo. Phir loop ke andar internal table se naam utha lo. Aur haan, FOR ALL ENTRIES se pehle table khaali to nahi, ye check karna mat bhoolna.

posts.caption:
Is your report taking 20 minutes instead of 2?

In most cases the cause is the same: a SELECT inside a LOOP. Every iteration is a separate trip to the database.

The fix: read the data once before the loop (JOIN or FOR ALL ENTRIES), then look it up in an internal table inside the loop. For large volumes, use a SORTED or HASHED table.
